messages.subject: NA removed automatically in ggplot2 0.9?
parts:
Hi dear all, 

It looks like now, NA is dropped when making a plot.  Here is the example, 

(p <- qplot(sleep_total, sleep_cycle, data = msleep, colour = vore))
unique(msleep$vore)  # contain NA

I am not sure if there is a way to keep extra NA in the plot and in the legend, so I can generally see distribution of those missing values.

Thanks

Tengfei

messages.subject: Re: NA removed automatically in ggplot2 0.9?
parts:
NA in aes variable is kept in plot but dropped from legend:

qplot(sleep_total, sleep_cycle, data = msleep, colour = vore, size =
I(10)) + scale_colour_discrete(na.value = "red")

messages.subject: Re: NA removed automatically in ggplot2 0.9?
parts:
Hi Kohske,

Thanks a lot, so is there a way to put NA in the legend too? because it's going to be a little hard to map data to legend for single plot when reader first see this plot. they would probably ask what's those gray points means. 

or current design just give general sense that all missing values in a colored plots are going to be in gray color? they will never be shown in the legend. It looks like sometimes points outside a limits are also rendered as gray color. 

I will eventually get used to this default anyway, it's just when I try to interpret the levels from legend like before, at first, I thought there is no NA in the data, and actually there is a small set of NA there. 

Tengfei

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: NA removed automatically in ggplot2 0.9?
parts:
Here is some discussion: https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/118

As the NA was (and is?) used for oob flag, it is difficult to handle
NA consistently.
But I see that NA has special meaning in data science, so the future
version of ggplot2 will handle NAs.

kohske
